chunks: O believers, do not nullify your charity by giving to oblige and flaunting (your favours) like a man who spends of his wealth only to show off, but does not believe in God and the Last Day. His semblance is that of a rock covered with earth which is washed away by rain exposing the hard rock bare. So they gain nothing from their earnings. God does not guide a people who do not believe.

key_terms.بِالْمَنِ: By expecting a return or favor

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between charity and nullified charity in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the spiritual danger of 'riya' (showing off) and 'adha' (causing hurt) which can nullify the reward of charity even if the act itself is valid. The metaphor of the 'smooth rock' (saffwan) signifies a deed that appears substantial but lacks the 'soil' of sincerity and faith, rendering it barren when tested by divine scrutiny. This underscores the Shia emphasis on the inner intention (niyyah) and the quality of the giver's demeanor as essential components of accepted worship.
